notes:
- Paint mask: with a tool picked, Shift+drag or holding the middle mouse button turns the view. Shift pressed after you start an ellipse or box still makes a circle or square.
- Paint mask: Find raised features finds the eyes (and any other bumps), ticks the two facing you and puts the mask round them; Mask reaches and Opening margin fine-tune it.
- Paint mask edges land exactly on the line you draw, however coarse the scan, and Smooth the surface keeps a low-detail scan's facets out of the mask. Tiny stray bits are left out.
- Paint mask: with no tool picked, dragging turns the view. Pick Ellipse, Box, Free line or Brush to draw; Esc puts it down.
- Paint mask: Clear mask also takes the built mask out of the view. Clearer names: Add and Subtract, Select facing side, Invert selection, Expand, Contract, Clear mask.
- The shell style Hug the latex is now called Contour Shell.
- Esc, when there's nothing else for it to cancel, asks whether to close GnomeShell.
- Paint mask (new Mask tab, or press 5): a thin cover that fits snug over the piece with openings to spray through, for painting the eyes after the piece is gray. Draw round the face with an ellipse, box or free line, then rub out each eye the same way (a brush touches up). Build paint mask saves a 3MF dome up, ready to slice. Thickness 1.2 mm and a 0.1 mm gap by default, with a fine edge round the openings for a crisp paint line.
- Tabs: every scan you open gets its own tab under the menus, so you can have several scans open and go between them. Each tab comes back the way you left it (cuts, view, step and build).
- Close a tab with the X on it, Ctrl+W or a middle click. It asks first; the scan and its cuts stay under Recent scans.
- + or Ctrl+T opens a new tab; Ctrl+Tab and Ctrl+Shift+Tab go to the next tab and the one before.
- The tabs you had open come back the next time GnomeShell starts.
- Builds wait their turn in a queue and run in the background, one at a time, so you can keep working in any tab while a shell builds. A tab shows a spinner while it builds and a green dot when it's done.
- Clean up scan (Scan tab): takes away the floor or table a phone or photo scan was made on, and anything else not joined to the latex mold, and closes it flat underneath. When a scan comes in with a floor, a banner offers it. Ctrl+Z puts the scan back.
- The test slice now goes through the whole model: every shell piece it crosses gets its own slice in that plane, so together they go all the way round. Drag the pink dot to move it.
- shell.3mf now holds every plate in one Bambu Studio project when the shell takes more than one plate (each plate is still saved on its own as plate 1.3mf, plate 2.3mf, ...). Open in Bambu Studio opens it. The same goes for test_slices.3mf when the slices take more than one plate.
- Phone scans: take photos of an object with the new GnomeShell Scan Android app and GnomeShell builds the 3D model on this PC, at its real size and standing upright. The Load scan screen has a Phone scans panel with the code for the app, the scan sheet to print, and each scan as it builds; press Open in GnomeShell when it's ready.
- The first phone scan downloads the free programs that do the work (COLMAP and OpenMVS, about 150 MB). See PHONE SCANS in READ ME.txt.
- Slice it for me (Cuts tab): one click lays out every cut. It tries cut 1 with the piece that has the most red split again and again, and thin layers (side to side, front to back, level, or each half of cut 1 in layers) with each layer kept whole or split its own way, and keeps the least overhang for the fewest pieces. Other layouts, under the button, has the best layout for each number of pieces. Ctrl+Z brings your old cuts back.
- Smallest piece (Settings, Printer & cutting, 7% of the shell by default): no suggested piece is smaller than this.
- Suggest more cuts is much faster (a second or two instead of up to a minute), finds less overhang, and keeps to Smallest piece.
- Draw a cut: pick the pencil in the tool rail (or press D) and drag a line across the model. The cut goes through the line straight away from you, only through the pieces the line crosses. Shift keeps it level, upright or at 45 degrees.
- The busy screen no longer blurs the view behind it, which could leave the view slow afterwards.
- One peg per joint when the model is split: one part gets the peg, the other the hole (a cut through two separate bits, like two legs, gets one in each).
- Draw a cut in Fit your printer: Free line, Box or Ellipse, then drag round the area you want as its own part. It cuts straight through the model the way you're looking, with pegs on the part inside and holes in the part round it.
- Pull the parts apart now shows the real parts: solid, with their pegs and holes. They're cut when you let go of the slider (nothing is saved until Split and save parts). Moving a cut puts the slider back to 0.
- Pull the parts apart: a slider under the cuts in Fit your printer spreads the model's own parts out in the view (the shell stays put). After Split and save parts it shows the saved parts with their pegs and holes.
- Bottom view (also after a build, or Ctrl+Numpad 7) so you can look under the shell and check the pegs sit in their slots.
- The insert mold is now one print: a thin 0.56 mm skin you tear off (Mold wall setting on the Insert tab), with a copy of the holder's core printed inside it. Pour silicone to the brim.
- New settings for the holder's arm width, frame width and thickness.
- One test slice for the whole mold, through the tallest point of the latex. Drag its pink dot in the view to move it.
- The insert holder's pegs always sit at the box's four corners, so the holder is a rectangle.
- Peg size on the Insert tab, and a Fit the pegs button that picks the biggest pegs that fit all four corners.
- A rectangle or oval insert kept sized to the latex keeps its shape: its width and depth fit the opening on their own.
- New look: menus (File, Edit, View, Help) and a toolbar along the top, an icon tool rail over the view with tips that name each tool and its key, and a status bar along the bottom.
- Scene list at the top right. After a build, every mold shell piece is in a Mold Shell folder, and a piece split to fit your printer gets a folder of its own inside it. The eye on a folder hides or shows everything in it; the eye on a row hides or shows just that part.
- X / Y / Z axes in the corner of the view turn with it. Click one to look down it.
- The legend and the overhang gauge sit along the bottom of the view, with counts.
- New keys: C add a cut, S scale box, R / Shift+R turn 90° / 15°, H hide the picked row in the Scene list, Alt+H show everything, X overhangs on or off, T test slices on or off, N hide the side panel, Ctrl+S save the layout, Ctrl+B build the shell.
